charts.s: A sharp run up, then a short, tidy drift lower. Buyers are resting, not leaving.
charts.buy: When price breaks above the top of the flag, ideally on a jump in volume.
charts.stop: Just under the lowest point of the flag.
charts.tgt: Add the height of the first run (the pole) to the breakout price.
charts.warn: If the flag gives back more than half the pole, it is not a flag anymore.

charts.s: A sharp drop, then a weak bounce that drifts up. Sellers are catching their breath.
charts.buy: Sell or avoid when price breaks below the bottom of the flag.
charts.stop: Just above the highest point of the bounce.
charts.tgt: Subtract the height of the first drop from the breakdown price.
charts.warn: If it climbs back above the top of the flag, the drop is probably done.

charts.s: A rounded dip back to an old high, then a small pullback before breaking out.
charts.buy: When price clears the handle and the old high (the rim).
charts.stop: Below the low of the handle.
charts.tgt: Add the depth of the cup to the breakout price.
charts.warn: A V-shaped cup or a handle that sinks into the bottom half of the cup is weaker.

charts.s: Sellers hold one price, but buyers keep stepping in higher. Something has to give.
charts.buy: When price closes above the flat top.
charts.stop: Below the most recent higher low.
charts.tgt: Add the height of the triangle at its widest to the breakout price.
charts.warn: A breakout on light volume often slips back inside.

charts.s: Buyers defend one price, but each bounce is weaker. Support usually cracks.
charts.buy: Sell or avoid when price closes below the flat bottom.
charts.stop: Above the most recent lower high.
charts.tgt: Subtract the triangle’s height from the breakdown price.
charts.warn: If it breaks above the falling line instead, sellers have run out.

charts.s: Highs get lower and lows get higher. Price coils, then usually breaks the way it was already going.
charts.buy: Trade the direction it breaks, once a candle closes outside the lines.
charts.stop: Just back inside the triangle, past the last swing.
charts.tgt: The height of the triangle at its widest, added from the breakout.
charts.warn: Breakouts near the very tip are less reliable. Fake moves are common.

charts.s: Price tests the same low twice and holds. A “W” that often ends a downtrend.
charts.buy: When price breaks above the middle peak of the W (the neckline).
charts.tgt: Add the distance from the lows to the neckline.
charts.warn: Two lows weeks apart are stronger than two lows days apart.

charts.s: Price fails at the same high twice. An “M” that often ends an uptrend.
charts.buy: Sell or avoid when price breaks below the dip between the two highs.
charts.tgt: Subtract the distance from the highs to the neckline.
charts.warn: Until the neckline breaks, it is just a stock taking a break.

charts.s: A high, a higher high, then a lower high. The uptrend is losing steam.
charts.buy: Sell or avoid when price breaks below the neckline (the line under both shoulders).
charts.tgt: Subtract the distance from the head down to the neckline.
charts.warn: Price often bounces back up to test the neckline once before falling.

charts.s: A low, a lower low, then a higher low. Sellers are getting tired.
charts.buy: When price breaks above the neckline (the line across both bounce highs).
charts.tgt: Add the distance from the head up to the neckline.
charts.warn: Wants rising volume on the right side. Without it, be skeptical.

charts.s: Price slides lower in a narrowing channel. Each drop is smaller. Sellers are fading.
charts.buy: When price breaks above the upper falling line.
charts.stop: Below the last low inside the wedge.
charts.tgt: Back to where the wedge started.
charts.warn: Can take a long time to resolve. Wait for the break, don’t guess it.

charts.s: Price climbs in a narrowing channel. Each push is weaker. Buyers are fading.
charts.buy: Sell or avoid when price breaks below the lower rising line.
charts.stop: Above the last high inside the wedge.
charts.tgt: Back to where the wedge started.
charts.warn: Common after a long run in a hot stock. Tighten stops if you own it.

charts.s: After a run, price moves sideways in a tight range for weeks, then breaks out.
charts.buy: When price clears the top of the range on strong volume.
charts.stop: Below the bottom of the range.
charts.tgt: A common goal is 20–25% above the breakout.
charts.warn: A range wider than about 15% is sloppy, not a base.

candles.s: Small body on top, long wick below, after a drop. Sellers pushed down hard and buyers shoved it back.
candles.means: The selling may be running out.
candles.act: Buy above the hammer’s high. Stop under its wick.

candles.s: Small body at the bottom, long wick on top, after a drop. Buyers are starting to test higher.
candles.means: An early hint the drop could turn.
candles.act: Buy above its high once confirmed. Stop under its low.

candles.s: A big green candle that completely covers the red candle before it.
candles.means: Buyers took over in one day.
candles.conf: Stronger on high volume and at a support level.
candles.act: Buy above the green candle. Stop under its low.

candles.s: Big red, a small pause candle, then big green. Three days that turn a downtrend.
candles.means: One of the more reliable bottoms.
candles.conf: The green candle closes past the middle of the red one.
candles.act: Buy near the third candle’s close. Stop under the small middle candle.

candles.s: After a red day, it opens lower but closes more than halfway up the red candle.
candles.means: Buyers erased most of the prior loss.
candles.act: Buy above its high. Stop under its low.

candles.s: Three strong green candles in a row, each closing near its high.
candles.means: A steady, real shift to buying.
candles.conf: Small wicks. Long upper wicks mean it is tiring.
candles.act: Buy a small dip after. Stop under the second candle.

candles.s: A small green candle tucked inside the previous big red one.
candles.conf: Needs a higher close next. Weaker on its own.
candles.act: Buy above the big red candle’s high. Stop under its low.

candles.s: Small body at the bottom, long wick on top, after a run. Buyers pushed up and got rejected.
candles.means: The rally may be running out.
candles.act: Sell or tighten your stop under its low.

candles.s: Looks like a hammer, but shows up after a run up. A warning, not a signal.
candles.means: Sellers showed up during the day.
candles.conf: A red candle that closes below it.
candles.act: Tighten your stop under its low.

candles.s: A big red candle that completely covers the green candle before it.
candles.means: Sellers took over in one day.
candles.conf: Stronger on high volume and near resistance.
candles.act: Sell or avoid. Stop above the red candle’s high.

candles.s: Big green, a small pause candle, then big red. Three days that turn an uptrend.
candles.means: One of the more reliable tops.
candles.conf: The red candle closes past the middle of the green one.
candles.act: Sell or avoid. Stop above the small middle candle.

candles.s: After a green day, it opens higher but closes more than halfway down the green candle.
candles.means: Sellers erased most of the prior gain.
candles.act: Sell or tighten your stop under its low.

candles.s: Three strong red candles in a row, each closing near its low.
candles.means: A steady, real shift to selling.
candles.conf: Small wicks. A long lower wick means it is tiring.
candles.act: Sell or avoid. Wait for a base before buying.

candles.s: Opens and closes at almost the same price. A cross shape.
candles.means: Buyers and sellers are tied. After a big run, that is a caution sign.
candles.conf: Means nothing alone. Watch what the next candle does.
candles.act: Wait. Trade the direction of the next candle.

candles.s: A small body with wicks on both sides.
candles.means: Indecision. The trend is losing push.
candles.conf: The next candle shows who won.
candles.act: Wait for the next candle before acting.
